The text does not make direct confirmation a necessary condition for using a supplier-capacity lead. The instructions say a supplier plan can "support a conditional view of supply or competition," and that "an unconfirmed deployment can be a lead: identify the missing link and what would resolve it, without asserting it exists." So a lead can be recorded while the missing link is named. My earlier note treated NVIDIA's direct-customer status as the link to resolve, which is consistent with that guidance, but the instructions do not require it before any use.

The instructions also say a supplier's revenue is not the covered company's revenue, so the lead cannot be read as NVDA orders or revenue. I did not rely on that point in the earlier note.

Two supplied statements relevant to checking the link:

1. The incoming quote: "adding 47 new machine centers in its Wuxi, China plant" for "NVIDIA AI data center racks." This names NVIDIA as the end market but not as a contracting party.
2. Item e2: "100% of this new capacity already pre-sold and tied to multi-year, multi-product awards." The awards are not attributed to named customers in the supplied text, so the customer identity is the missing link.
